key_insight: A privacy-preserving distillation framework can transfer clinically useful multimorbidity reasoning from large language models into smaller models without exposing real patient data.
clinical_relevance: The distilled scores improved survival prediction on UK Biobank data, suggesting LLM-based methods could enhance large-scale risk stratification in health systems.
method: Used state-of-the-art LLM teacher models to generate multimorbidity reasoning.
Distilled knowledge into compact CoLLM student models using synthetic cohorts matched to UK Biobank distributions.
Evaluated transfer quality and downstream performance without direct access to sensitive patient records.
evidence_signal: Knowledge transfer was strong (Spearman rho 0.75–0.89), with LLM-as-Judge confirmation and downstream gains including C-index up to 0.91 and heritability around h2 ≈ 0.05.
watch_item: Performance may vary substantially across teacher models, so results could depend on model choice and careful validation before deployment.
paper_title: Privacy-Aware Distillation of Large Language Models for Enhanced Multimorbidity Scoring
